As early as next month, Apple is expected to launch a redesigned next-generation MacBook Pro. We can expect to see OLED displays, the first touchscreen in the Mac lineup, a thinner chassis, the Dynamic Island, and many more new features. Previous rumours had suggested this upgraded version would be named the MacBook Ultra, but the future of the MacBook Pro branding has remained unclear. Now, however, things have become much clearer.

Initially, everyone assumed that the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with the M5 chip would retain the MacBook Pro name. Later, Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reported that Apple would also bring several elements of the MacBook Ultra design to the entry-level MacBook Pro equipped with the M7 chip. To me, this significantly reduces the likelihood of the "MacBook Ultra" naming being used.

However, the latest report makes the idea of the MacBook Pro and MacBook Ultra coexisting in the product lineup much more plausible.

According to Omdia, Apple will continue producing its existing miniLED display panels until 2028.

This means two things: first, if the current MacBook Pro remains in the lineup, the new redesigned model will very likely require a significant price increase; at the same time, the new model is almost certainly going to be named the MacBook Ultra.

Therefore, for roughly the next year or so, the MacBook lineup is likely to look as follows:

Autumn 2026:

  • MacBook Neo (A18 Pro)
  • MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M5)
  • MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch, M6)
  • MacBook Pro (miniLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)
  • MacBook Ultra (OLED, 14-inch and 16-inch, M5 Pro and M5 Max)

Spring 2027:

  • MacBook Neo (A19 Pro)
  • MacBook Air (13-inch and 15-inch, M6)
  • MacBook Pro (OLED, 14-inch, M7)

Summary

If this all comes true, the MacBook lineup will be the largest it has ever been. Ultimately, the days of the older MacBook Pro remaining in the lineup are not expected to last very long. I suspect this is part of Apple's strategy to maintain a lower starting price, consistent with their approach in the past.

Under this scenario, I expect the starting price of the miniLED MacBook Pro to remain at around US$2,499, while the Ultra's starting price will be higher, likely US$2,999.

What do you think of this rumoured MacBook lineup? What starting price do you expect for the MacBook Ultra? Let us know in the comments section.
